title: Call of Duty Was Built by the Team Behind Medal of Honor
hook: Twenty-two developers finished Medal of Honor: Allied Assault in 2002, walked out, and founded Infinity Ward. Activision bought 30 percent of them before they had shipped a single game. Twenty-three years later, Modern Warfare 4 launched this Friday. Did you play the first Call of Duty back in 2003?
sources: https://gamespot.com/2866756/ (GameSpot, E3 2002: Activision signs Infinity Ward)
https://investor.activision.com/node/15401 (Activision press release, Oct 14 2003: release date Oct 29, team of 20+ Allied Assault developers)
script: Did you know the studio behind Call of Duty was founded by twenty two people who had just finished Medal of Honor? In January of two thousand two, Electronic Arts released Medal of Honor: Allied Assault on PC. It was a big hit, made by a small studio called Twenty Fifteen. Within months, a large part of that team had left. Grant Collier and Vince Zampella set up a new company called Infinity Ward, and Jason West joined them. Twenty two Allied Assault developers made up the team. At E3 in two thousand two, Activision announced it had bought thirty percent of the brand new studio, with an option to buy the rest. Its first project was another World War Two shooter, and it arrived on PC on October twenty ninth, two thousand three. It was called Call of Duty. Activision liked it so much that it bought the remaining seventy percent of Infinity Ward within days of launch. Twenty three years later, that series is one of the biggest in gaming. And this week Infinity Ward shipped Modern Warfare Four, which launched on Friday, October twenty third. So the team that made Medal of Honor ended up building its biggest rival. Did you play the original Call of Duty back in two thousand three? Follow for more gaming history.
